sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Dated December 11, 2025. Announces GPT-5.2 Pro available that day in the Responses API as gpt-5.2-pro, alongside Thinking and Instant. Adds configurable reasoning and xhigh for Pro. Exact Pro benchmark columns do not report production parameter counts or architecture.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 Pro model
sources.evidence: Exact model page and its Markdown edition identify gpt-5.2-pro-2025-12-11, a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 maximum output tokens, text/image input, text output, reasoning effort medium/high/xhigh, Responses-only access and function calling. No production parameter counts or architecture are specified.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts input_file items. For vision-capable models, PDF processing supplies both extracted text and page images. This applies to the exact Pro model through its documented Responses and image-input support; PDF is a supported file format, not an additional native sensory modality.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Original December 11, 2025 system card was downloaded and text-extracted. Its training and evaluation account concerns GPT-5.2 Instant and Thinking. It does not identify exact Pro weights, total/active counts, or an explicit shared-checkpoint relation that would justify transferring Thinking architecture.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
sources.evidence: Later comparison tables label GPT-5.2 Pro separately, including GDPval 74.1%, GPQA Diamond 93.2% and other benchmark results. The exact Pro columns and pricing row provide no total/active production parameter count or architecture.

sources.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
sources.evidence: April 23, 2026 report names GPT-5.2 Pro in its methods and Supplementary Table 2. It evaluates Pro variants with a separate Pro harness and reports 10.8% pass rate for GPT-5.2 Pro. It does not specify production parameter counts, architectural structure or shared weights with Thinking.

sources.title: Prompt caching 201
sources.evidence: Guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Explains prompt caching as key/value tensors in Transformer attention layers and heads, and lists gpt-5.2 in its model table. It does not independently establish an exact gpt-5.2-pro-to-gpt-5.2 checkpoint relationship.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 model
sources.evidence: The separate gpt-5.2 model page explicitly lists prompt_caching. This corroborates caching for Thinking, not a structural inference for the separately identified Pro model without an explicit underlying-model relationship.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement grants limited use of hosted services while reserving service intellectual-property rights to OpenAI (section 9.1). Together with the exact model being supplied through paid OpenAI API/ChatGPT access, supports descriptive proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes — June 12, 2026
sources.evidence: The June 12, 2026 entry explicitly retires GPT-5.2 Instant, Thinking and Pro from ChatGPT, migrating existing conversations to corresponding GPT-5.5 models. This is a ChatGPT retirement, not an API shutdown statement.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.evidence: Current complete Markdown deprecation listing was checked for the exact Pro alias and dated snapshot. It contains GPT-5.2 Chat and Codex shutdown entries but no exact gpt-5.2-pro or gpt-5.2-pro-2025-12-11 shutdown entry. Absence of a notice does not independently test endpoint operation.

name.note: Exact developer name; distinct from GPT-5.2 Thinking and Instant.

family.note: The launch places Pro within the GPT-5.2 series; replaces the generic gpt-pro grouping.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public release found: December 11 announcement says API access is available that day. The exact dated snapshot agrees; ChatGPT rollout timing does not delay the API release.

open_weights.note: Exact model is distributed as a proprietary hosted API/ChatGPT service; no downloadable checkpoint is supplied in these primary release and model materials.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification, not an SPDX identifier or a claim that the current service agreement was the launch-day version.

parameters_b.note: No total production parameter count is given in the reviewed original Pro release/API material, original family training card, later exact Pro comparison tables or GeneBench methods. Benchmark scores and higher inference compute are not model-size evidence.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count is disclosed for exact GPT-5.2 Pro in the reviewed primary material. A separate Pro harness or longer reasoning does not establish MoE routing, an active count or additional weights.

architecture.note: Exact-model searches covering first-party training and interpretability material, the original system card, later Pro comparisons and GeneBench found no verifiable Pro structure. The base gpt-5.2 supports Transformer KV caching, but no explicit Pro-to-that-checkpoint relationship was established. Neither inference compute nor absence of Pro cached pricing establishes or rules out Transformer/MoE structure.

context_window.note: Exact Pro page labels 400,000 as context window and separately 128,000 as maximum output. No independent maximum input is derived by subtraction; the >128k input rate-limit tier is not the context maximum.

modalities.note: Native documented inputs are text and image, with text output. Add PDF as an API-supported file input via Responses vision processing. Image-generation tool support does not make image a native model output, and no native audio/video support is asserted.

reasoning.note: Exact GPT-5.2 Pro supports reasoning tokens and medium, high, xhigh effort. The original GPT-5 Pro high-only limitation and the Thinking model none/low options do not apply here.

tool_call.note: Exact Pro documentation lists function calling, file search, image generation, MCP and web search through Responses. Function calling is directly documented, not inferred from benchmark performance.

description.value: GPT-5.2 Pro reasoning model with text and image input, function calling, and a 400,000-token context window.
description.note: Replace subjective higher-accuracy/tougher-workflow wording with directly documented capabilities.

patch.description: GPT-5.2 Pro reasoning model with text and image input, function calling, and a 400,000-token context window.
patch.notes: API snapshot: gpt-5.2-pro-2025-12-11. Documented context window: 400,000 tokens; maximum output: 128,000 tokens. Supports reasoning effort medium, high and xhigh through Responses. PDF input is processed into text and page images. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed in the reviewed sources; Pro architecture remains unverified. ChatGPT retired GPT-5.2 Pro on June 12, 2026. No exact Pro API shutdown notice was found in the current deprecation list; endpoint operation was not tested.

notes: Independent exact-variant review. Original and later exact Pro tables and first-party research were inspected; targeted training/interpretability searches did not verify architecture. Shared architecture with Thinking is not assumed. Current API documentation and deprecation notices are documentary evidence, not a live endpoint test.
summary: Correct family to gpt-5.2, classify license as Proprietary, add supported PDF input, and replace subjective description. Confirm December 11, 2025 release, exact snapshot, 400K context, 128K output, medium/high/xhigh reasoning and function calling. Keep total/active counts undisclosed and architecture unverified. Distinguish June 12, 2026 ChatGPT retirement from API status.
